title: prune-orphan-workflows-and-introduce-ci-dependency-verifier
author: Priya Menon
release_notes: Remove stale workflows, centralize CI orchestration, add a fast-failing dependency drift checker to block transitive upgrades; no user-facing changes.
description:
Context: Over time we accumulated a handful of orphaned GitHub Actions workflows and several duplicated lint/test job definitions across the monorepo. This PR prunes stale workflows, centralizes common job templates, pins a small set of transitive action versions, and adds a lightweight CI job (ci/verify-deps) that fails fast when transitive dependency snapshots drift beyond a controlled whitelist. Motivation: reduce CI flakiness, speed up matrix cold-starts, and make dependency churn visible to engineers before it reaches release branches. Changes in this PR:
- Remove three stale workflows: .github/workflows/ci-nightly-legacy.yml, .github/workflows/old-release-pipeline.yml, .github/workflows/test-integration-legacy.yml (these were not referenced by any teams since 2024 and were creating sporadic runs).
- Create .github/workflows/ci-orchestration.yml as a single entrypoint that dispatches job templates via workflow_call to keep surface area small.
- Add .github/actions/templates/lint-test-template.yml and refactor several repo workflows to call it (reduces duplication and ensures consistent env).
- Add a script scripts/ci/verify_deps.sh and a job in ci-orchestration.yml: verify-deps. The job computes a compact transitive tree (yarn/npm/pip where applicable) and compares against an approved snapshot in .ci/dependency-snapshots/. The job currently checks: node_modules lockfile drift for SDK packages and Python wheel version bounds used by the private installer.
- Pin a small set of Actions (checkout@v4, setup-node@v4, actions/cache@v4) and bump some action usages to reduce transient failures from upstream breaking changes.
- Update docs/ci/README.md with the new template usage and the process to update dependency snapshots (ci/README snippet).
Checklist:
- [x] Remove orphaned workflows and verify no active runs reference them
- [x] Centralize lint/test job into template and update callers
- [x] Implement verify-deps job with snapshot comparison and whitelist override (manual approval file .ci/whitelist.txt)
- [x] Add tests for verify_deps.sh (unit-level smoke)
- [x] Document rollback steps and owner list for snapshot updates
How to review: Focus on ci-orchestration.yml and scripts/ci/verify_deps.sh. The template refactor touches many workflows but each caller is a one-line change to use workflow_call; the template lives under .github/actions/templates. Testing done: ran the new orchestration locally via act (light smoke), executed verify_deps.sh against the venv and a prepared lockfile, and validated on a feature branch that the CI matrix cold-start time dropped ~25% in our sample. CI history: first CI run (2026-02-20) flagged a lint rule mismatch because one repo still referenced an old eslint config; fixed by commit that updated package.json scripts. Final CI run (2026-02-25) shows all checks green. Rollout plan: merge to main and monitor ci-run durations for one week; if any jobs start flaking, revert by reverting the workflow file or temporarily setting ci-orchestration.yml to skip template calls and run a fallback flow. Follow-ups (tracked separately): ENG-3199 (automate snapshot updates via daily bot), ENG-3205 (add Python/Go snapshot comparators), and a small cleanup PR to unify action pins across other repos. Links: internal runbook: https://linear.app/redwood/issue/ENG-3121/ci-orchestration-and-dep-verifier, docs PR template: https://github.com/redwood/.github/pull/---.

review_thread: Jordan Lee (2026-02-21): Can we narrow the initial verify-deps scope to SDK packages only? I don't want the job to block platform infra updates.
Priya Menon (2026-02-21): Good point. I updated the script to accept --scope and set default to 'sdk' in the workflow. We can expand later.
Samir Kulkarni (2026-02-22): The template looks good; one nit on using secrets.NPM_TOKEN in the template — we should document required secrets for repo callers.

merge_outcome: Merged to main via rebase. Post-merge verification: monitored first 12 main CI runs, observed median cold-start improvement from 42s -> 31s for matrix jobs; no new flakiness reported in the first 48 hours. Owners: @infra-team, @platform-sre.
notes: This PR deliberately keeps the dependency snapshot checker in fast-fail mode and behind a whitelist to avoid blocking release lanes while we iterate on comparator coverage. If you need to update a snapshot, edit .ci/dependency-snapshots/* and add a short justification to .ci/whitelist.txt; owners will review.
